metadata.title: Causal Couture Week 10 — Reliability Reconciliation
metadata.continuity: Direct continuation of Causal Couture Week 9; no persistent week badge.
metadata.methodological_boundary: The reliability review is an interpretation layer over existing diagnostics, not a causal estimator, replacement diagnostic, reliability score, or source of causal proof.
metadata.production_gate: Direct clean-master production authorized after internal QC; no separate review/slate export unless correction is required.

beats.narration_text: Hi, my name is Ushasvi Rachel, and this video is about reliability reconciliation and evidence interpretation in Causal Couture. Week 9 introduced a heuristic unobserved-confounding sensitivity analysis. Week 10 asks how the growing collection of Phase 5 reliability evidence should be interpreted together.

shot.visual_intent: Integrated presenter introduction and Week 9-to-10 transition.

beats.narration_text: Phase 5 already included the adjusted effect, row and SKU-cluster bootstrap uncertainty, shuffled-treatment placebo testing, temporal falsification, overlap, stockout diagnostics, model robustness, unobserved-confounding sensitivity, and observational evidence reporting. Each tests a different potential weakness.

As the stack grew, independent outputs became harder to interpret. Diagnostics returned estimates, uncertainty, warnings, statuses, and different limitations. Week 10 asks: what does the reliability evidence look like when all diagnostics are reviewed together?

shot.visual_intent: Multiple diagnostic outputs converging on one interpretation question.

beats.narration_text: The new module is causal_reliability_review.py. It is not a causal estimator, a replacement for existing diagnostics, or a source of causal proof. It is an interpretation layer reviewing availability, limitations, sensitivity findings, and areas requiring investigation.

The review distinguishes three categories. Successful diagnostics returned usable results. Inconclusive diagnostics lacked sufficient analytical evidence because of data or model conditions. Failed diagnostics encountered processing or implementation errors requiring investigation.

shot.visual_intent: Successful, inconclusive, and failed status cards.

beats.narration_text: An unavailable or inconclusive diagnostic is not evidence for or against the primary estimate. Possible causes include insufficient observations, inadequate treatment variation, missing columns, insufficient analytical conditions, or execution errors. These are possible conditions, not claimed Week 10 failures.

shot.visual_intent: Unavailable-not-evidence distinction and possible status conditions.

beats.narration_text: The reliability review also incorporates the Week 9 unobserved-confounding sensitivity findings. That diagnostic tests the estimate across Weak, Moderate, Strong, and Very Strong hypothetical stress scenarios, then examines whether the estimated direction remains stable or changes under the modeled pressure.

shot.visual_intent: Sensitivity scenarios flowing into the Week 10 review.

beats.narration_text: Directional stability is relatively robust only within the tested synthetic conditions. A direction change suggests sensitivity to modeled assumptions and deserves scrutiny. Neither result discovers a real confounder, measures hidden bias, estimates its probability, or establishes causal identification.

shot.visual_intent: Conservative two-path interpretation with methodological boundaries.

beats.narration_text: The causal-intelligence response now includes reliability_review alongside estimation and diagnostics. A dedicated GET slash phase five slash causal reliability review endpoint exposes this layer for inspection, testing, reporting, and visualization.

shot.visual_intent: Consolidated response and dedicated API endpoint.

beats.narration_text: The architecture preserves two layers. The estimator asks: what effect does the model estimate? The reliability review asks: how much caution should surround it? Future diagnostics can join without fundamentally changing primary estimation.

Bootstrap procedures examine estimation uncertainty. SKU-level cluster bootstrap accounts more carefully for repeated product observations. Shuffled-treatment placebo testing examines behavior after destroying the original treatment structure. Temporal falsification examines behavior in an impossible causal direction.

Overlap checks meaningful comparisons. Stockout diagnostics examine inventory constraints. Robustness compares specifications. Sensitivity applies hypothetical omitted-variable pressure. These test different assumptions. Multiple successes do not prove causality. Observational evidence, methodological robustness, and proven causal effects are not equivalent.

shot.visual_intent: Second diagnostic matrix and three-way evidence distinction.

beats.narration_text: Implementation added causal_reliability_review.py, updated causal_intelligence.py and main.py, and prepared reliability-focused validation support. The changes were integrated and pushed to the project repository. Detailed numerical diagnostic and endpoint results remain separate from this report.

Week 10 delivered reconciliation, structured status interpretation, sensitivity integration, the reliability_review field, a dedicated endpoint, and preserved observational boundaries. The project is shifting from individual checks toward a unified reliability assessment framework.

The question is no longer only the estimated effect. It is also what evidence supports it, what is incomplete, and where caution remains. A model producing an estimate is not the same as sufficiently reliable evidence for a strong causal interpretation.

shot.visual_intent: Estimate-to-interpretation progression and final methodological takeaway.
